section.sectionSummaryBrief: Although the level of transformation (It'hapcha) is generally higher than suppression (It'kafya), suppression has a unique advantage in that it specifically draws down the hidden treasure of the Awtsmoos, as illustrated by the parable of a king who spends all his treasures to win a war.
section.t: Now, although the aspect of It'hapcha (transformation) is,
in general,
far more elevated than the aspect of It'kafya (suppression),
nevertheless, there is also an advantage in the aspect of It'kafya over the aspect of It'hapcha.
This is understood from what is said in Tanya,
that the concept of a "servant of G-d" is specifically when he suppresses and changes his nature,
and this advantage is not present in a complete tzaddik.
And specifically through the service of It'kafya, "the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is elevated in all worlds,"
the drawing down and revelation of the light that is in the aspect of loftiness,
as is explained at length in the discourse of the day of the Hilula,
with a parable of a mortal king who, for the sake of victory in war, spends all his treasures,
for in normal years, not only does he not use them for anything, but they are hidden and sealed from the eye of any beholder,
and specifically at the time of war, not only does he open all the treasures,
but moreover, he spends them without any measure or limit, and gives them to the soldiers in order to win the war.
And the analogy for this Above,
is that there is an aspect of a treasure that is hidden and sealed from the eye of any beholder,
"No eye has seen, O G-d, besides You,"
and in order to win the war against the evil inclination,
the service of It'kafya,
they also give this treasure,
and in a manner of squandering,
and the giving of the treasure is specifically to the simple soldiers,
for since their service is with self-sacrifice beyond the measure and limit of intellect, therefore the giving of the treasure to them is also in a manner of squandering beyond all measure and limit.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: In the future, the Exodus from Egypt will still be mentioned because the advantage of It'kafya—drawing down the hidden treasure—will be needed, and it will be revealed in its ultimate perfection.
section.t: Based on this, one can understand why they will mention the Exodus from Egypt even in the future,
even though the revelations of the future are more elevated
(wondrous)
than the revelations that were in the Exodus from Egypt,
for since the drawing down of the aspect of the treasure is specifically for the sake of victory in war,
and in the future there will be no war with the evil inclination, for "the spirit of impurity I will remove from the earth,"
therefore,
they will mention the Exodus from Egypt even then,
in order that there will also be the advantage of It'kafya,
the drawing down of the aspect of the treasure.
And this drawing down will also be in ultimate revelation then
(like all matters of the future),
and "your Teacher will no longer be hidden."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The future redemption will combine both advantages—the suppression (It'kafya) of the Exodus and the transformation (It'hapcha) of wondrous revelations—achieved through our service in exile with self-sacrifice, leading to a revelation without garments and from below.
section.t: And this is "As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders,"
that in the future redemption there will be both advantages,
the advantage of It'kafya,
"As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt,"
and the advantage of It'hapcha,
"I will show him wonders."
For through our deeds and service during the time of exile,
the general service of the time of exile being in a manner of self-sacrifice beyond measure and limit,
for in the time of exile, and especially in the footsteps of Moshiach, there are obstacles and hindrances and many trials,
even to the trial of not being ashamed before people who mock him,
and nevertheless, they pay no attention to all the hindrances,
and they study Torah and fulfill mitzvos without any calculations,
to the extent that even "the empty ones among you are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate,"
meaning not only do they fulfill mitzvos, but they are full of mitzvos,
behold, through this they leave exile with great wealth of mitzvos and great wealth of Torah
[for Torah study is also a mitzvah,
and moreover,
it is equivalent to all the mitzvos],
and since this
(the great wealth of Torah and mitzvos)
adds to merit, it also adds haste to "I will hasten it,"
and in a manner of "behold, with the clouds of heaven,"
that very soon there will be the true and complete redemption,
and in a manner of "As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders," meaning there will be both advantages.
For since the redemption comes through our deeds and service during the time of exile,
and especially in the footsteps of Moshiach,
therefore it will be "As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt,"
the advantage of It'kafya,
and together with this there will also be "I will show him wonders,"
wonders even relative to the wonders
(signs and wonders)
that were in the Exodus from Egypt,
including also the wonders that were at the time of the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds,
for although at the Splitting of the Sea there were most elevated revelations,
as "each one pointed with his finger and said, 'This is my G-d, and I will glorify Him,'"
to the extent that "a maidservant saw at the sea what the prophets did not see,"
nevertheless, all this was at the sea,
clothed in the aspect of Malchus
[similar to the revelation of the Exodus from Egypt
(before the Splitting of the Sea)
which was "on the opening"],
and also the revelation of the Splitting of the Sea was only temporary,
for the revelation then was from Above, and the lower realm had no vessel for it,
in general, it is a matter of It'kafya and not It'hapcha
[similar to the Exodus from Egypt, which was in a manner of "for the people fled"].
Because this did not come from the service of the lower realm.
However, in the future there will be "I will show him wonders,"
wonders even relative to the wonders that were in the Exodus from Egypt and the Splitting of the Sea,
that the revelation will be without any garment and also from the side of the lower realm,
and together with this there will also be the advantage of "As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt,"
speedily in our days, literally,
with the coming of Moshiach our righteous one.
